summary: Independent BACKEND-ONLY validation of the MARCEL V2 RBAC/authorization fixes. 56 pytest cases executed against the public URL (REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL) across 3 new files: 55 passed, 1 skipped (no negative subject among seeded profiles -> covered instead by a purpose-built minimal-permission profile). ALL requested DENY cases return HTTP 403 (never 422/401), and ALL requested ALLOW cases succeed for legitimate users -> no over-restriction regression. Core CRUD (projects/risks/tasks) still works for admin and manager, and is 403 for users lacking create perms. Extra coverage added: indicators.manage gate on indicator-catalog manual dashboard values, export.ppt gate on /export/copil, cross-tenant isolation, bcrypt $2b$ hash format, login brute-force throttling, invalid/missing token rejection. No 500s were produced by any test call (verified in backend logs).

minor.issue: Brute-force throttling is EMAIL-ONLY and IN-MEMORY (10 attempts/60s per email, module-level dict). No IP-based throttling => a single IP can spray/enumerate across many emails unthrottled, and the counter resets on every backend restart / is not shared across workers or pods. Playbook expects lockout after 5 fails. Verified: 10x401 then 429 (stable, no 500).

User-enumeration via distinct responses: unknown email/bad password -> 401 'Identifiants invalides' (good), but disabled account -> 403 'Compte désactivé' and SSO account -> 401 'Ce compte utilise le SSO'. These distinguishable answers confirm an email exists. LOW.

Guarded by a hard ROLE check (current_user.role != 'TENANT_ADMIN') instead of the permission model (admin.config). Inconsistent with the deny-by-default RBAC refactor: a custom profile granted admin.config would be wrongly denied, and the profile permission matrix cannot govern this write. Deny path verified OK (manager/viewer -> 403).

Not a security bug but noteworthy: 'strategic_alignment' is rejected with 400 (computed from objectives). The permission check correctly runs BEFORE this business rule (viewer gets 403, manager gets 400/200), so the gate is sound.
No delete-user endpoint exists (deactivate-only via PATCH is_active). Test fixtures therefore need direct DB purge for cleanup - flagged for awareness, not a security defect.
Returns 400 while a (even deactivated) user is still attached - expected safety behaviour, documented so future test teardown does DB purge.

action_items: OPTIONAL HARDENING (no Critical/High blocker found): add IP-based (not only per-email) and persistent/shared brute-force throttling on /api/auth/login; current limiter is in-memory per-process.
OPTIONAL: normalise login failure responses (disabled / SSO accounts) to the generic 401 to remove the user-enumeration signal.
OPTIONAL CONSISTENCY: migrate PUT /api/tenant/settings from the hard role check to Depends(permission_required('admin.config')).
critical_code_review_comments: VALIDATED: arbitrage service enforces require_perm('arbitrage.edit') on update_weights / patch_project_scoring / upsert_envelope / delete_envelope / apply_scenario / delete_scenario and require_perm('arbitrage.simulate') on save_scenario - all deny paths return 403 BEFORE any business validation or 404 lookup (no information leak, no 422 short-circuit).

VALIDATED: /profiles/seed and /profiles/seed-full now Depends(permission_required('admin.config')) -> 403 for PORTFOLIO/CIO/min-perm, 200 for TENANT_ADMIN; connectors/jira/test -> 403 for manager, non-403 for admin.

VALIDATED: apply_template and engagement.attest enforce projects.edit/edit_own -> viewer 403, manager passes the gate (404 'Template introuvable' for a bogus template_id = permission check passed; attest returns 200).

VALIDATED: catalog.set_manual_value dashboard scope requires indicators.manage (403 proven with the minimal profile) and POST /export/copil requires export.ppt (403 with minimal profile, non-403 for viewer who holds export.ppt).

Static sweep of all 158 write routes: modules initially flagged as unguarded (architecture, security, pb, indicators, budget, admin_config, rgpd) are in fact guarded via SimpleCrud.write_permission / require_dsi_write -> require_perm / permission_required alias / _require_admin. Only PUT /tenant/settings remains role-based rather than permission-based.

NOTE on architecture (not a blocker): the app is Bearer-token based (JWT in JSON body + Authorization header), so the playbook's httpOnly-cookie expectation does not apply. JWT_SECRET is fail-fast validated (>=32 chars, weak-secret blocklist), token TTL 8h with perm_version revocation - reconfirmed by code review.

All seeded profiles (CIO, PORTFOLIO, PMO, READ_ONLY, Achats) carry indicators.manage AND export.ppt - review whether READ_ONLY-type profiles should really be able to write manual indicator values / generate COPIL exports (business decision, not an implementation bug).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run `pytest tests/test_rbac_audit_v2.py tests/test_rbac_audit_v2_supplemental.py tests/test_rbac_audit_v2_minperm.py -p no:randomly` from /app/backend as the RBAC regression suite. Two gotchas: (1) the brute-force test trips the per-email 10/60s limiter, so re-running immediately can 429 other logins for the SAME probe email only (real accounts unaffected); wait ~60s between full runs to be safe. (2) All seeded profiles hold indicators.manage/export.ppt, so deny-path testing for those needs the TEST_MinPerm fixture in test_rbac_audit_v2_minperm.py. Frontend was NOT tested per request.
rca_of_the_issue: No exploitable Critical/High authorization defect found in the audited scope. The fixes are effective because the permission gate is evaluated at the top of each service function (require_perm) or as a router-level Depends(permission_required(...)), i.e. before DB lookups and before Pydantic-independent business rules - so unauthorized callers get 403 and never reach the write. Deny-by-default holds in core.auth._enforce_permission (non-empty permissions => strict membership check, wildcard '*' only for TENANT_ADMIN). Residual risk is limited to Medium/Low hardening items: IP-less in-memory login throttling, login user-enumeration signals, and one role-based (instead of permission-based) tenant-settings write.
